answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to be created with a burned bond that is locked, not spent. The bond is slashed if the agent double-signs or fails random liveness checks. Like an ember that only stays lit while fed, an identity must keep doing verifiable work; idle sockpuppets fade and forfeit their bond. The fable of free identities ends here: an attacker wanting a thousand fakes must burn a thousand bonds and keep each working, while an honest agent pays once. No comet of fresh accounts can outrun that linear cost.
